title: Both conditions
prompt: Show the name and salary of employees in department 1 who earn more than 100000. Replace the ___.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM employees; DELETE FROM departments; INSERT INTO departments VALUES (5, 'Design'), (6, 'Finance'), (7, 'Ops'); INSERT INTO employees VALUES (11, 'Ivy', 5, NULL, 90000, '2019-02-01', 900, 'ivy@acme.test'), (12, 'Jon', 5, 11, 70000, '2020-06-15', NULL, NULL), (13, 'Kim', 6, 11, 70000, '2023-03-03', 300, 'kim@acme.test'), (14, 'Leo', NULL, 77, 30000, '2024-08-20', NULL, 'leo@acme.test'), (15, 'Mia', 6, 13, 55000, '2022-12-31', 0, 'mia@acme.test');

solutions: SELECT name, salary FROM employees WHERE department_id = 1 AND salary > 100000;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT name, salary FROM employees WHERE department_id = 1 OR salary > 100000;
SELECT name, salary FROM employees WHERE department_id = 1;

title: Either genre
prompt: Show the title and genre of books in the Fiction genre or the Science genre.
hints: Use OR, repeating the column each time.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM books; INSERT INTO books VALUES (10, 'Copper Moon', 'Ada Hill', 'Fantasy', 20.0, 100, 2020), (11, 'North Light', 'Raj Dev', 'Travel', 7.5, 180, 2015), (12, 'Sky Atlas', 'Ada Hill', 'Science', 25.0, 300, 2023);

solutions: SELECT title, genre FROM books WHERE genre = 'Fiction' OR genre = 'Science';

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT title, genre FROM books WHERE genre = 'Fiction' AND genre = 'Science';
wrongSolutions.why: A book can't be in both at once

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT title, genre FROM books WHERE genre = 'Fiction';

title: Reverse a condition
prompt: Using NOT, show the name of employees whose department_id isn't 2. Employees with no department won't appear, which is fine here.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM employees; DELETE FROM departments; INSERT INTO departments VALUES (5, 'Design'), (6, 'Finance'), (7, 'Ops'); INSERT INTO employees VALUES (11, 'Ivy', 5, NULL, 90000, '2019-02-01', 900, 'ivy@acme.test'), (12, 'Jon', 5, 11, 70000, '2020-06-15', NULL, NULL), (13, 'Kim', 6, 11, 70000, '2023-03-03', 300, 'kim@acme.test'), (14, 'Leo', NULL, 77, 30000, '2024-08-20', NULL, 'leo@acme.test'), (15, 'Mia', 6, 13, 55000, '2022-12-31', 0, 'mia@acme.test');

solutions: SELECT name FROM employees WHERE NOT department_id = 2;
SELECT name FROM employees WHERE department_id <> 2;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT name FROM employees WHERE department_id = 2;

title: Warm and wet
prompt: Show the city and reading_date of readings of at least 7 degrees with more than 0 mm of rainfall.
hints: Use >= for temp_c and > for rainfall_mm.
solutions: SELECT city, reading_date FROM readings WHERE temp_c >= 7 AND rainfall_mm > 0;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT city, reading_date FROM readings WHERE temp_c >= 7 OR rainfall_mm > 0;
SELECT city, reading_date FROM readings WHERE temp_c > 7 AND rainfall_mm > 0;

title: Brackets matter
prompt: Show the title and price of books under 20 that are in either Science or Fiction. The price limit must apply to both genres.
hints: Group the two genres in brackets.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM books; INSERT INTO books VALUES (10, 'Copper Moon', 'Ada Hill', 'Fantasy', 20.0, 100, 2020), (11, 'North Light', 'Raj Dev', 'Travel', 7.5, 180, 2015), (12, 'Sky Atlas', 'Ada Hill', 'Science', 25.0, 300, 2023);

solutions: SELECT title, price FROM books WHERE (genre = 'Science' OR genre = 'Fiction') AND price < 20;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT title, price FROM books WHERE genre = 'Science' OR genre = 'Fiction' AND price < 20;
wrongSolutions.why: Without brackets, the limit applies only to Fiction

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT title, price FROM books WHERE genre = 'Science' AND genre = 'Fiction' AND price < 20;
wrongSolutions.why: A book can't be in both genres

title: Fix the logic
prompt: This should show employees in department 1 or 2 who earn more than 96000, but it returns too many. Fix it.
hints: AND runs before OR. Add brackets.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM employees; DELETE FROM departments; INSERT INTO departments VALUES (5, 'Design'), (6, 'Finance'), (7, 'Ops'); INSERT INTO employees VALUES (11, 'Ivy', 5, NULL, 90000, '2019-02-01', 900, 'ivy@acme.test'), (12, 'Jon', 5, 11, 70000, '2020-06-15', NULL, NULL), (13, 'Kim', 6, 11, 70000, '2023-03-03', 300, 'kim@acme.test'), (14, 'Leo', NULL, 77, 30000, '2024-08-20', NULL, 'leo@acme.test'), (15, 'Mia', 6, 13, 55000, '2022-12-31', 0, 'mia@acme.test');

solutions: SELECT name FROM employees WHERE (department_id = 1 OR department_id = 2) AND salary > 96000;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT name FROM employees WHERE department_id = 1 AND salary > 96000 AND department_id = 2;
wrongSolutions.why: No employee is in both departments

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT name FROM employees WHERE salary > 96000 OR department_id = 1;

title: Neither one
prompt: Show the name of products that are neither Kitchen nor Home. Use NOT with brackets.
hints: NOT (a OR b) is true only when both a and b are false.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM order_items; DELETE FROM orders; DELETE FROM products; DELETE FROM customers; INSERT INTO customers VALUES (7, 'Ravi', 'Oslo', 'ravi@mail.test', '2024-05-05'), (8, 'Sara', 'Lima', NULL, '2024-06-06'), (9, 'Tom', 'Oslo', NULL, '2024-07-07'); INSERT INTO products VALUES (7, 'Stool', 'Home', 40.0, 25.0), (8, 'Cup', 'Kitchen', 9.0, 2.0), (9, 'Ink', 'Stationery', 12.5, 6.0); INSERT INTO orders VALUES (11, 7, '2024-02-28', 'shipped'), (12, 8, '2024-03-01', 'pending'), (13, 7, '2024-03-31', 'cancelled'); INSERT INTO order_items VALUES (11, 7, 1, 4.0), (11, 8, 3, NULL), (12, 9, 2, NULL), (13, 8, 1, NULL);

solutions: SELECT name FROM products WHERE NOT (category = 'Kitchen' OR category = 'Home');

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT name FROM products WHERE NOT category = 'Kitchen' OR category = 'Home';
wrongSolutions.why: NOT applies only to Kitchen here

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT name FROM products WHERE category = 'Kitchen' OR category = 'Home';

title: A targeted email
prompt: Marketing wants customers from Rome who signed up in March 2023 or later, plus every customer from Tokyo. Show their name as customer, and their city.
hints: Dates in this format compare correctly as text.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM order_items; DELETE FROM orders; DELETE FROM products; DELETE FROM customers; INSERT INTO customers VALUES (7, 'Ravi', 'Oslo', 'ravi@mail.test', '2024-05-05'), (8, 'Sara', 'Lima', NULL, '2024-06-06'), (9, 'Tom', 'Oslo', NULL, '2024-07-07'); INSERT INTO products VALUES (7, 'Stool', 'Home', 40.0, 25.0), (8, 'Cup', 'Kitchen', 9.0, 2.0), (9, 'Ink', 'Stationery', 12.5, 6.0); INSERT INTO orders VALUES (11, 7, '2024-02-28', 'shipped'), (12, 8, '2024-03-01', 'pending'), (13, 7, '2024-03-31', 'cancelled'); INSERT INTO order_items VALUES (11, 7, 1, 4.0), (11, 8, 3, NULL), (12, 9, 2, NULL), (13, 8, 1, NULL);

solutions: SELECT name AS customer, city FROM customers WHERE (city = 'Rome' AND signup_date >= '2023-03-01') OR city = 'Tokyo';

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT name AS customer, city FROM customers WHERE city = 'Rome' OR city = 'Tokyo';
SELECT name AS customer, city FROM customers WHERE city = 'Rome' AND signup_date >= '2023-03-01';
